sections.title: Progress bar drawing and colors
sections.what: Takes a progress number, caps it between 0 and 100, and draws a rounded bar filled to that percentage. Shows an optional label and percentage, and chooses the color from a named list or a custom style class.
sections.why: Likely reason: capping the number keeps the bar from overflowing, and named colors keep meanings consistent across screens.
sections.watch_out: If both progress and value are passed, progress wins, and a value that is not a number, such as NaN, can show as a broken width.

summary: A thin rounded bar that fills to show a percentage, with an optional label and percentage text.
purpose: Show how far along something is, such as a goal or course.
why: Likely reason: one shared bar keeps progress displays consistent, and the value is capped to stay inside the bar.
how: 1. Takes a progress number, or a fallback value, and caps it between 0 and 100. 2. Picks a color from a named list, or uses a custom style class if one starts with the background prefix. 3. Draws the optional label and percentage above the bar. 4. Draws the bar with the filled portion set to the capped percentage.
inputs: A progress number from 0 to 100, or a fallback value; optional label, color name, extra class names and percentage display flag.
outputs: A visual bar on screen. Nothing is saved.
risks: A value that is not a real number, such as NaN, makes the bar width invalid. If a progress value is given, it wins over the fallback value.
debug: If the bar looks empty or full unexpectedly, check the number passed in. If the color is wrong, check the color name against the list. If a custom color is ignored, check that it starts with the background prefix.
